prompt.context: Our client is a private equity firm interested in Molds R Us, a small company that makes plastic moldings for houses in Russia. They want to know if we think investing in this company is a good idea. The firm also wants to understand what the 2011 market for moldings, particularly in plastics, will look like. The PE firm wants to see growth of 20% in the first year to justify this purchase. This company only plays in the Russian market and the PE firm is not interested in expanding across borders. This company is the only player in plastic moldings. Moldings are used where walls meet the ceiling to add a decorative appeal to houses and are only used in residential buildings. All housing starts require moldings in the year they are started, and are all completed by the next year.
prompt.question: Should the PE firm invest in Molds R Us? Estimate the 2011 market size for plastic moldings in Russia and assess whether the company can achieve 20% revenue growth in its first year.

clarifying_info.q: How much does a contractor charge to install moldings?
clarifying_info.a: A contractor makes on average 50 Rubles per hour.

clarifying_info.q: How fast can a contractor lay down moldings?
clarifying_info.a: A contractor can lay down 1,000 feet of molding per hour.

clarifying_info.q: What is the average wall length per house?
clarifying_info.a: The average house has 4,000 meters of walls.
DIY (self-installation) is only possible for rubber moldings; PVC plastic and wood and plaster all require a contractor.

exhibits.title: Types of Moldings
exhibits.shows: A comparison table of five molding options (No Moldings, PVC Plastic, Rubber, Wood, Plaster) across three attributes: price per 10 meters, installation requirements, and replacement cycle.

exhibits.title: Moldings Used in the Russian Market
exhibits.shows: Two data series: (1) market share by molding type (stacked percentages) for 2005-2010, and (2) total residences and housing starts by year for 2005-2010.

framework: Understand the market: size, growth rate, and competitive landscape for moldings in Russia
Assess Molds R Us's position: market share, product focus (PVC plastic only), pricing vs. competitors
Estimate 2011 market size for plastic moldings: existing homes replacing + new housing starts
Calculate market growth rate (existing homes ~2%/yr vs. new starts ~30%/yr) and weight by segment contribution
Test against the 20% growth hurdle: can plastic molding revenues plausibly grow 20% YoY?
Synthesize: investment recommendation with key risks and next steps

questions.prompt: Analyze Exhibit B: what trend do you observe in PVC plastic molding market share from 2005 to 2010?
questions.guidance: A strong candidate notes that PVC plastic market share is essentially flat (25-26%), while rubber moldings show rapid share gains (0% to 12%). The overall housing market is growing but plastic's share is not. This signals that Molds R Us, as the sole plastic molding player, is not capturing incremental demand.

questions.prompt: Calculate the overall market growth rate for existing homes and new housing starts from 2005 to 2010.
questions.guidance: Candidate should compute two separate growth rates, recognize that existing homes dominate the market (~85%), and therefore blend them to see overall market growth is far below 20%.

math.setup: Existing homes CAGR: (33.1M - 29.7M) / 29.7M / 6 years. New starts CAGR: (1.25M - 0.45M) / 0.45M / 6 years.
steps: Existing homes growth rate: (33.1M - 29.7M) / 29.7M = ~11.4% total over 6 years => ~2% per year
New starts growth rate: (1.25M - 0.45M) / 0.45M = ~178% total over 6 years => ~30% per year
Existing homes are ~85% of the market (1.7M existing vs. 0.35M new starts; see next calculation), new starts ~15%
Blended growth: 0.85 * 2% + 0.15 * 30% = 1.7% + 4.5% = ~6.2% per year — well below 20%
math.answer: Overall blended market growth is approximately 6-10% per year, well short of the required 20% hurdle.

questions.prompt: Estimate the total meters of PVC plastic moldings expected to be sold in 2011.
questions.guidance: Candidate must account for: (1) 2011 total residences = 2010 residences + 2010 starts; (2) apply 25% plastic share to existing homes, then divide by 5 (replacement cycle); (3) estimate 2011 housing starts and apply 25% share for new construction demand; (4) multiply total plastic houses by 4,000 meters per house.

math.setup: 2011 residences = 33.1M + 1.25M = ~34.3M. Apply 25% plastic share. Divide existing by 5 (replace every 5 years). Estimate 2011 starts ~1.4M (extrapolating trend), apply 25%. Multiply by 4,000 meters.
steps: Existing homes replacing in 2011 (1/5 cycle): 8.575M / 5 = ~1.715M houses
Total houses needing plastic moldings in 2011: 1.715M + 0.35M = ~2.065M houses
Total meters: 2.065M * 4,000 meters = ~8.26 billion meters (approx. 8.2B meters)
math.answer: Approximately 8.2 billion meters of PVC plastic moldings will be sold in 2011.

questions.prompt: Given your analysis, should the PE firm invest in Molds R Us? Provide your recommendation.
questions.guidance: Strong candidate synthesizes: plastic market share is stagnant, overall housing growth is modest, blended growth is ~6-10% which is far below the 20% hurdle. Recommend against the investment in its current form, and optionally suggest alternatives (rubber moldings, operational improvements).

brainstorming.prompt: What alternative strategies or investments could the PE firm consider given this analysis?

categories.name: Alternative acquisition targets
ideas: Look at rubber molding companies given rapidly rising market share (0% to 12% in 5 years)
Consider consolidating multiple small players in the fragmented no-moldings segment

categories.name: Operational improvements at Molds R Us
ideas: Invest in sales and marketing to increase plastic market share
Expand distribution channels to reach more contractors
Introduce contractor incentive programs to drive plastic preference
Explore product line extension into rubber moldings

categories.name: Pricing and product strategy
ideas: Compete more aggressively on price vs. rubber (1 Ruble vs. 1.5 Rubles already favorable)
Bundle installation services to reduce total cost of ownership
Highlight durability advantages of PVC vs. rubber (5-year vs. 7-year cycle)

recommendation: The PE firm should NOT purchase Molds R Us at the current terms
PVC plastic molding market share has been flat at ~25-26% for five years, showing no growth momentum

Even with strong housing starts growth (~30%/yr), existing homes dominate the market (~85%) at only ~2%/yr growth; the blended rate (~6-10%) falls well short of the required 20% first-year growth threshold
risks: If rubber moldings continue gaining share, plastic's 25% could erode further
Rising contractor labor costs (currently 50 Rubles/hr) could make plastic less competitive vs. DIY rubber
Dependency on Russian residential market creates geographic concentration risk
next_steps: Investigate rubber molding companies as acquisition targets, given their rapid market share growth
Conduct a deeper sales and marketing audit of Molds R Us to quantify upside if distribution and contractor relationships are improved
Model whether a combination of price reduction and increased marketing spend could realistically deliver 20% growth within a revised investment thesis
